answers.question_text: Define the OSI reference model. Name its seven layers and state one function of each.
answers.transcript: The OSI model is a seven-layer reference architecture that divides network communication into layers. The physical layer transmits bits, the data link layer handles framing and error control, and the network layer routes packets. The transport layer provides end-to-end delivery, the session layer manages dialogs, the presentation layer translates and encrypts data, and the application layer provides services to the user.

key_points.text: OSI is a seven-layer reference architecture; each layer provides a service to the layer above and uses the layer below
The seven layers are Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, and Application
Each layer has a well-defined function such as bit transmission, framing, routing, end-to-end delivery, dialog control, translation, or user services

answers.question_text: Differentiate circuit switching and packet switching.
answers.transcript: Circuit switching establishes a dedicated physical path before the transfer and keeps it for the whole call, so bandwidth is reserved even when nobody is speaking. Packet switching breaks data into packets and forwards them independently with store-and-forward, sharing links statistically. Circuit switching is good for continuous voice, while packet switching is good for bursty data traffic.

key_points.text: Circuit switching establishes a dedicated physical path for the entire communication; packet switching sends independent packets using store-and-forward
Circuit switching reserves bandwidth even during idle periods; packet switching shares links statistically
Circuit switching suits continuous voice traffic; packet switching suits bursty data traffic

answers.question_text: Explain the TCP three-way handshake used to establish a connection.
answers.transcript: The client sends a SYN segment with its initial sequence number. The server replies with a SYN-ACK that acknowledges the client ISN and carries the server's own initial sequence number. The client then sends an ACK for the server ISN, and the connection is established. Both endpoints have now synchronized their sequence numbers. The exchange also prevents an old duplicate connection request from being accepted. A labelled diagram shows the client and server states for SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK.

key_points.text: Client sends a SYN segment carrying its initial sequence number
Server replies with SYN-ACK, acknowledging the client ISN and sending its own ISN
Client sends ACK acknowledging the server ISN, and the connection is established
Both endpoints synchronize their initial sequence numbers
The handshake prevents an old duplicate connection request from being accepted
A labelled client/server diagram shows the SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK exchange
